title: Tenant Thaw Controller and Warm Fallback Playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Context:
This doc is a working PRD for a feature we’re calling the Tenant Thaw Controller (TTC). It ties together autoscale gating, controlled opportunistic burst, and a tenant-level soft-sabbatical mechanism that lets cold tenants be thawed in a predictable, latency-safe manner while protecting noisy neighbors and preserving headroom for committed tenants.

Problem statement (short):
- Customers on Dedicated want predictable tail latency for high-priority tenants even when overall cluster utilization spikes and others attempt bursts.
- Current autoscalers either over-provision (cost) or under-react (latency spikes) for cold-starty tenant patterns (batching-heavy jobs, periodic cron workloads, dev/test bursts).
- Need operational controls to: 1) allow planned/short opportunistic bursts, 2) thaw cold tenants incrementally, and 3) quarantine/soft-shelve tenants when they destabilize pools.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce P95 token latency regressions for committed tenants during mixed-workload surges by >= 40% vs baseline.
- Limit additional reserved GPU minutes due to warmups to <10% of committed usage for steady-state customers.
- Provide operators and customers a clear, auditable state machine for tenant thaw/shelve events (>= 95% event visibility in Console).

Non-goals:
- This is not a wholesale replacement for commit-based autoscaling or our predictive warm pool. It’s an intermediate runtime controller focused on tenant-level graceful thawing and temporary burst governance.

User personas / user stories:
- Platform engineer (enterprise customer): "I need my core APIs to keep P95 under 500ms even on peak traffic and be able to stamp out noisy tenant behavior without manual ops."
- Solutions engineer (Redwood): "I want a knob to limit how many new KV cache fills or pre-warms happen simultaneously during a ramp to avoid cross-tenant tail effects."
- SRE on Redwood ops: "When a large customer does a scheduled job that thaws many workers, I want automated staged thawing and circuit breakers so autoscaler doesn’t spin an entire pool at once."

Key concepts / glossary (quick):
- Thaw: process of bringing a tenant from cold (no preloaded KV/cache/warm workers) to warm; may include prefetch, KV population, or container/GPU warm slots.
- Thaw wave: a controlled cohort of tenant endpoints (or shards) allowed to warm concurrently.
- Soft-shelve / Sabbatical: temporary, reversible restriction that limits a tenant’s capacity or delays thawing when they exceed destabilization thresholds.
- Opportunistic burst: short-lived allowance for extra concurrency served from spare capacity with stricter latency SLOs and possible degraded fidelity model variants.

Design overview:
1) Tenant Thaw Controller (runtime component)
- Input signals: per-tenant recent QPS, queue latency, KV miss rate, cold-start counts, priority tier (committed vs best-effort), linked reservation credits.
- State machine: COLD -> PENDING-THAW -> THAWING -> WARM -> SOFT-SHELVED. Transitions annotated with metrics and operator triggers.
- Thaw waves: configurable wave_size and inter-wave-delay. Default wave_size = min(10% of target concurrency, 8) with backoff on observed P95 degradation.

2) Autoscale handshake and preflight checks
- TTC will call autoscaler in two phases: preflight reserve (soft token allocation) and confirm commit. Preflight reserves are ephemeral and do not consume customer billing until confirm.
- If preflight shows resource contention, TTC delays waves and optionally downgrades opportunistic burst to lower-fidelity model (if available) or queues requests to fallback route.

3) Opportunistic burst lanes
- Spare-capacity pool (opportunistic pool) that can be loaned for short bursts. Loans come with metadata: max-duration, token budget, and a priority flag that allows immediate soft-throttle if tail effects observed.
- Billing: tracked separately; customers are warned and can opt-in to use opportunistic lanes (default OFF for enterprise).

4) Isolation and soft-shelving controls
- Detection: rapid increases in per-tenant KV miss rate, disproportionate concurrency growth, or repeated preflight failures trigger a soft-shelve candidate.
- Soft-shelve action: reduce tenant concurrency quota by X% (configurable), move to best-effort fallback route for new requests, and rate-limit warm operations for N minutes with exponential backoff.
- Operator override: console action to lift or force-shelve with audit log.

API / Console surfaces (sketch):
- Tenant config fields: thaw_wave_size, thaw_backoff_ms, opportunistic_burst_enabled (bool), opportunistic_budget_tokens, soft_shelve_thresholds (list of metrics).
- Console runbook: visual timeline of thaw waves, current state, and per-wave P95/P99. Quick actions: abort thaw, pause, force-thaw, apply soft-shelve.
- Alerting: new alert type "tenant-thaw-degradation" with suggested runbook steps.

Operational behaviors and runbook (ops):
- Normal thaw: TTC allows wave, autoscaler confirms, warm workers spin, KV prefetch runs, and wave marked WARM if P95 impact < threshold.
- If P95 spikes > threshold: throttle next wave, optionally move older waves to lower concurrency, send alert.
- If repeated failures (>3 waves): mark tenant SOFT-SHELVED, notify customer, provide remediation steps (reduce concurrency, schedule off-peak thaw).

Metrics / success criteria (instrumentation):
- Per-tenant P95, P99 before/during/after thaw wave (tagged by wave id).
- KV miss ratio delta and warm-worker spin time distribution.
- Number of soft-shelve events (goal: low false positives).
- Resource delta from preflight to confirm (wasted preflight allocations) — target < 8% of total preflight requests.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal): TTC enabled for internal test tenants only; observability + manual overrides. Target: 2 weeks.
- Beta (select customers): opt-in via dedicated tenant flag; collect telemetry, tune wave sizing, expose soft-shelve notifications via console. Target: 8–12 weeks.
- GA: enabled as an opt-out safety net for all dedicated clusters; docs + runbook + support training.

Edge cases and tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: conservative waves reduce tail impact but increase end-to-end time for cold tenants. Need clear SLAs for thawed latency vs warm-latency.
- Cost: preflight reserves can create apparent demand — implement strict TTLs and LRU for preflight allocations.
- Multi-tenant co-warm: collocated tenants warming together may still interact; use stochastic staggering and affinity-aware wave selection to minimize.
notes: Open questions: how to surface opportunistic burst costs in per-token billing line items? Do we expose thaw controls to self-serve customers? Need SRE runbook tie-ins for manual evacuations. Also consider integrating with Optimize to suggest wave sizes per workload fingerprint. Next steps: spike implementation in simulator + integration test harness.
